items.title: Straight From the (AI) Source: Is AEO/GEO different than SEO?
items.summary: Google, Microsoft, and Perplexity state that AEO/GEO optimization mirrors traditional SEO: high-quality content, structured data, no spam. AI uses RAG grounded in search indexes, so good SEO covers AI visibility. Avoid shortcuts like content chunking to prevent penalties.

items.title: Literary agents ban use of AI in book submissions
items.summary: Several literary agencies, including Greene & Heaton, the Bright Agency, the Eve White Literary Agency, and Janklow & Nesbit, have updated their submission guidelines to ban the use of generative AI in cover letters, synopses, proposals, and manuscripts, rejecting such submissions due to the increasing prevalence of AI-generated content. The reasons cited include the risk of suppressing an author's unique voice and the ethical concerns surrounding AI's potential 'theft' of copyrighted material from writers to train models, as highlighted by lawsuits against companies like Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta, and Microsoft. This ban implies that authors must submit original work to be considered, potentially limiting access to assistance tools and emphasizing the industry's commitment to authentic human creativity.

items.title: HATER FRIDAY | Mass-Generating Literary Slop: AI-Written Books
items.summary: The opinion strongly opposes the influx of AI-written books in publishing, particularly in the romance genre, as exemplified by author Coral Hart who used AI to produce over 200 novels in 2025, many completed in just 45 minutes. Key arguments against AI books include their inability to capture human emotions, resulting in shallow and soulless content that relies on overused tropes and clichés. Additionally, AI writing lacks subtlety, forces interpretations through blunt phrasing, plagiarizes common expressions, and produces trivial conflicts with no meaningful character development or depth.

items.title: BookTok Gets a Bad Rap
items.summary: BookTok has received criticism for promoting derivative and trashy content, but it also features high-quality books like 'One of Us Is Lying' by Karen M. McManus, a thriller blending elements of 'The Breakfast Club' and 'Sherlock Holmes,' and 'All the Bright Places' by Jennifer Niven, which maturely explores teenage trauma. The platform has driven trends such as the rise of Romantasy, estimated to have earned $610 million, and boosted authors like Colleen Hoover to bestseller status through social media buzz. Despite controversies over unoriginal works, BookTok's recommendations have led to discoveries of engaging young adult stories, encouraging deeper exploration beyond surface-level judgments.

items.title: ‘A Knight of Seven Kingdoms’ Actress Responds to Racial Backlash About Her Role
items.summary: Tanzyn Crawford, playing Tanselle in HBO's A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms, addressed online backlash over her casting due to her race, noting the intimidation of joining the franchise but affirming her right to pursue her dreams. Social media criticism arose as some viewers expected the show, focused on white male characters, to remain 'non-woke.' George R.R. Martin confirmed she matched his vision for the character from The Hedge Knight.

items.title: Woke Crowd Backlash Over Scary Movie 6 Pronoun Joke in Trailer
items.summary: The Scary Movie 6 trailer, spoofing modern horror with the original cast, ignited controversy with a joke where a character corrects 'she' to 'they' after a stabbing. Online debates erupted over the satire targeting pronouns and cancel culture. The film's edgy humor draws comparisons to Scream franchise issues.

items.title: ‘Sinners’ Takes Top Prize at the Actor Awards
items.summary: Ryan Coogler's Sinners won best ensemble and Michael B. Jordan took outstanding male actor at the 32nd Actor Awards, upsetting previous frontrunners. The film positions strongly for Oscars after victories over One Battle After Another. Harrison Ford received the Life Achievement Award.

items.title: NAACP Image Awards: ‘Sinners’ Dominates Amid BAFTA Slur Controversy
items.summary: Sinners swept the 57th NAACP Image Awards, winning outstanding motion picture and multiple acting awards for Michael B. Jordan, Miles Caton, Wunmi Mosaku, and Delroy Lindo. The event addressed a BAFTA incident where a racial slur was shouted at Jordan and Lindo during a presentation. Celebrities used speeches to highlight anti-Black racism and political issues.

items.title: Netflix Announces March 2026 Releases Including Peaky Blinders Movie
items.summary: Netflix's March lineup features Peaky Blinders: The Immortal Man with Cillian Murphy reprising Tommy Shelby in a WWII-era story. Other highlights include One Piece Season 2, Virgin River Season 7, sci-fi War Machine, and BTS content. The Peaky Blinders feature marks a major return for the popular series.

items.title: AI’s Impact on the Small Business Employment Landscape
items.summary: Gusto payroll data from over 400,000 small businesses shows that AI-exposed workforces are linked to revenue gains of about $53,800 annually for typical firms and slight increases in hiring, rather than job losses. The overall mix of AI-exposed work has remained stable at around 16.3-16.4% since early 2023, with AI impacting existing jobs through tools and workflows instead of major workforce changes. However, younger workers aged 22-28 in highly AI-exposed roles have experienced declining headcount, while older workers see gains.

items.title: IBM Shares Plummet 13%—Worst Day Since 2000—After Anthropic Launches Programming AI Tool
items.summary: Anthropic announced a tool for its Claude Code that helps modernize COBOL code, a legacy language used in critical business systems like ATMs and Social Security payments. This new AI tool aims to address the shrinking pool of COBOL experts by automating updates to billions of lines of production code. The launch triggered a sharp selloff in IBM shares and broader software stocks, highlighting AI's disruptive potential for business technology services.

items.title: How Agentic AI Will Transform Consumer-Driven Companies in 2026
items.summary: Agentic AI is evolving from passive prediction tools to autonomous systems that execute complex actions across consumer touchpoints, from discovery to post-purchase support. Small businesses are adopting AI rapidly, with nearly 60% usage—double from 2023—and high adopters seeing 84% gains in sales and profits. To thrive, small brands must optimize catalogs for AI, adopt answer engine optimization, and partner with tech providers for visibility.
